ratings_why.fun: Laying eggs and watching chicks land and heave on the hour is a joy to grow, though the low cards are mostly one keyword and the clock asks a lot of the reader.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because its power lives inside the enemy's units: eggs ride their hosts, and one clock both sides speed up decides when it pays out; no tribe today plays on the other board like that.

verdict_why: v3 closed the last ordering gaps; what is left is text density and UI, which more passes would only shuffle.

points.text: Frau Wechselbalg carries the tribe-wide hatch order (your hosts first, then theirs). Move that line into the Egg keyword so her card only says what she does.

Little Gernegroß is the longest card in the tribe. Most of it could become a keyword like "Hide: become an Egg in the enemy across; your slot waits for you", leaving the triple-stats hatch on the card.
The clock counting both sides' attacks is the one thing a player can't see on the cards. A dial with three pips between Chimes on the fight screen would make the whole tribe readable.
Mother Rohrsang bends Lay to aim at a friend. Showing her eggs in her own colour would tell foster chicks from heaving chicks at a glance.
Ottilie reads cleanly now that her repeats come after Chime effects. A short tag on each repeated card ("on the hour") would show players which effects she picks up.

standouts.why: Pipit-Moor Hen: two words of text, and it teaches the whole tribe's fantasy on turn one.
Little Gernegroß hiding in the enemy and hatching three times his size is the cuckoo story told in play.
Red-Mouth: one line, a huge payoff, and pure begging-chick flavour.

weakest.why: Weight-Hanger is a plain death trigger with little cuckoo or dormouse feel beyond its name.
Old Unruh speeds the clock for both sides, which is hard to read as help in a mirror and gives the opponent's Chimes too.
Frau Wechselbalg is a strong idea buried under rules text about order and duplicate names.

flags.note: With Ottilie, Hawk-Barred Hen re-Dozes the enemy across at every Chime, so it never attacks; killing the Hen is the only answer.
Bellows beside Herald of Spring doubles a permanent +2/+2 to every Clockwork each fight.
Red-Mouth with Ottilie and several Hens floods Heaves each strike; the design already flags it.
